age_seconds.description: Age of the data at response time

as_of.description: When the data was read from the ledger

ledger_index.description: Validated ledger the data comes from

stale.description: True when served past its fresh TTL (stale-on-error)

blackholed.description: True when the master key is disabled, there is no signer list and no usable regular key, so the account can never sign again

currency.description: Canonical currency code (3 characters or 40 hex)

currency_ascii.description: Readable text of a 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

domain.description: Issuer domain decoded to text, when set

obligations.description: Total issued of this currency; null when `obligations_status` is `unavailable`

tick_size.description: The issuer's `TickSize` (3 to 15 significant digits in offer exchange rates), null when unset

description: Issuer data for an issued asset: flags, domain, transfer fee and total issued. When to use: Before accepting or sending an issued token: check that the issuer exists, is not frozen, whether holders need authorization, and the transfer fee charged on every transfer between non-issuer accounts. Prefer another tool: For XRP (not an issued asset; 400), for one account's own balances use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`, and for prices use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`. Example: xrpl_token {"asset":"USD.rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B"} Paid: 0.02904 USDC or 0.0242 EURC per call on Solana mainnet, VAT included. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.02 EUR-denominated units (approx 50 calls per bundle) or 0.024 USD-denominated units (approx 34 calls per bundle).

asset.description: Issued asset, never XRP. Currency format: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.
